title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover ordering (load-shedding stability)
author: Aisha Khan
description: Background: we saw recurring incidents where the SLO enforcer entered aggressive backoff and regional failover ordering caused thrashing under load (see ENG-3729). This PR stabilizes the enforcer by tightening hysteresis, smoothing threshold transitions, and fixing a race in the regional failover ordering path that could cancel backoff timers and cause repeated failovers. Changes are limited and safe for hotfix: 1) introduce a minimum hysteresis window (2000ms) and exponential backoff cap for per-region enforcer decisions; 2) add threshold smoothing (moving average over last N windows) to prevent rapid toggles on noisy metrics; 3) serialize regional failover ordering decisions via a lightweight ordering lock to avoid races that cancelled active backoff timers; 4) add metrics and tracing hooks to observe decision path; 5) add unit/integration tests and a canary deployment plan. Testing: unit tests added for hysteresis and smoothing logic; integration test in perf-canary simulates regional outage + burst load to validate no failover thrash; manual canary deployed to us-west-2 then gradually scaled to other regions. Rollout: squash-merge to main and immediate canary; monitoring dashboard updated and alert thresholds relaxed for noisy metrics. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced issue locally and in perf-canary - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] CI green after second run - [x] Docs/observability updated - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR comments
